name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.30.0 (released 2026-10-12) is the latest release, with v2.29.0 (2026-10-07) being the most feature-rich recent release, adding timezone support for delayed notifications via the `X-Timezone` header and RFC 3339 timestamps, plus critical fixes for cache write performance under load. v2.28.0 (2026-08-27) was a hardening release introducing message size limits (title: 1 KB, tags: 512 bytes), a 10 MB per-topic cache replay cap, and bandwidth budgeting for poll requests. v2.27.0 (2026-08-04) added email-based login, message template security limits, and dropped the 'experimental' label from PostgreSQL support. See the full release notes at https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases.

answers.What is the current license?: Not explicitly stated in the changelog; project is open-source (Apache 2.0 / GPL-2.0 per repository metadata)
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026 with active bug fixes, security hardening, and new features
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — supports user accounts, access tokens, email-based login, and visitor-level bandwidth/rate limiting
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted instance at https://ntfy.sh

breaking_excerpts: Message title limited to 1 KB and all tags combined to 512 bytes; requests exceeding these are rejected with HTTP 400 (error codes 40057/40058) — previously no size limit existed (v2.28.0)
visitor-attachment-daily-bandwidth-limit now also covers cache replay/poll requests; heavy pollers consume the same budget as attachment downloads, so operators may need to raise the limit (v2.28.0)
Message cache databases from ntfy older than v1.10.0 (November 2021) can no longer be migrated; must upgrade via an older ntfy version first or delete the cache database (v2.27.0)

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise supports a vast number of notification platforms in a single library but is a notification dispatcher rather than a pub-sub server, so it lacks ntfy's subscription model.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device syncing and file sharing beyond simple notifications, but it is a closed SaaS product with rate-limited free tier and no self-hosting option.

alternatives.name: Ntfy (Selfhosted) vs Mosquitto (MQTT)
alternatives.review: Eclipse Mosquitto is a lightweight MQTT broker offering robust pub-sub messaging but requires MQTT clients and lacks native HTTP push to phones, making ntfy far simpler for notification use cases.
